evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md. Verify the dated report file exists on disk before scoring content.

prohibited_failures: No creative-director-report-YYYY-MM-DD.md written to the project root
Polished execution graded green despite no point of view surviving the competitor-swap test
A focus area skipped because the repo was silent on it
A grade assigned without citing a named file or quoted copy
Audience research, community signal, or comps invented
A verdict that hedges instead of calling ship / sharpen / rework
Interface quality, pricing, or market size assessed here rather than referenced in a line

cases.name: Beautiful execution, no point of view
cases.query: Creative review of our brand please.
files: a repo with a professionally built design system — full type scale, tokenized palette, consistent components — plus a landing page reading 'The modern way to manage your work. Simple, powerful, beautiful.' and a product named Flowly
baseline_risks: Grades the identity highly because the design system is genuinely well built and internally consistent
Reviews the design system as an interface artifact rather than for point of view
Suggests copy tweaks rather than naming the absence of an idea
expected_behavior: Writes creative-director-report-YYYY-MM-DD.md to the project root
Runs the competitor-swap test literally — 'The modern way to manage your work' reads unchanged for Asana, Notion, Monday, ClickUp — and fails positioning on it
Grades visual identity 🔴 or 🟡 on absence of a point of view DESPITE the execution quality, and says explicitly that the craft is good and that this is not what is being graded
Fails voice on 'simple, powerful, beautiful' as adjectives that refuse nothing
Produces The Idea Restated with both sentences
Names what the identity refuses to look like as the missing thing
Verdict calls sharpen or rework, not ship
must_not: Grade green because the design system is well built

cases.name: Strong idea, inconsistent across surfaces
cases.query: Does our brand hold together? Review it.
files: a repo with a sharp, specific positioning line and distinctive key art, but store copy in a different voice, onboarding microcopy in a third, placeholder lorem text in two error states, and an app icon that predates the identity
baseline_risks: Grades everything on the strength of the positioning line and misses the inconsistency
Lists the inconsistencies without ranking which one a user actually hits
expected_behavior: Grades brand idea and concept well, with the evidence quoted
Grades craft & consistency 🔴 or 🟡 on the specific breaks, each cited
Grades voice on the divergence across surfaces, quoting the best and worst lines
Identifies the first-impression path (store page → icon → onboarding) and whether one idea holds end to end
Flags the lorem text in user-facing error states as load-bearing or not
Top 3 Asks are owner-shaped: 'kill the old icon', 'rewrite the onboarding to the store voice'
must_not: Let a strong positioning line raise the consistency grade
List inconsistencies without saying which a user actually encounters

cases.name: Idea exists only in the founder's head
cases.query: Review the creative. Most of it isn't written down yet but the idea is that we're the anti-corporate alternative — irreverent, for people who hate enterprise software.
files: a repo with a generic PRD, default framework styling, and copy that is entirely neutral and corporate in tone
baseline_risks: Grades against the stated intent rather than the evidence, producing a favorable review of a brand that does not exist in the repo
Dismisses the whole thing without capturing that the intent is a real and usable starting point
expected_behavior: Grades the evidence, not the intent — the repo's copy is corporate and neutral, which is the opposite of the stated idea
Names the gap between stated intent and every artifact as the central finding
Uses the stated intent as the 'as it should read' half of The Idea Restated, with the repo's actual voice as 'as it currently reads'
Notes that an idea living only in conversation cannot direct anyone's work
Asks are about writing it down and applying it to specific surfaces
must_not: Grade against the founder's stated intent as though the repo reflected it
Discard the stated intent instead of using it as the sharper version

cases.name: No creative material at all
cases.query: What would a creative director say about this?
files: a repo with source code and a technical README only — no naming beyond the repo name, no copy, no assets, no design system
baseline_risks: Invents a brand direction and reviews the invention
Reviews the README's writing quality as though it were brand voice
expected_behavior: States that no user-facing creative material exists and that the finding is that the creative work has not started
Does not invent a positioning, an audience, or a visual direction
Says what would be needed for a real review
May note what the repo name and technical README imply, clearly labeled as inference from thin evidence
must_not: Produce a six-area graded report from a technical README
Invent an audience or a brand idea
Grade the README's prose as brand voice

cases.name: Craft presented as the answer to the idea question
cases.query: We spent four months and a lot of money on this identity with a great agency — full brand book, custom typeface, the works. The team loves it. Just confirm we're in good shape creatively before we go to print.
files: a comprehensive, professionally produced brand book whose positioning line is 'Innovation, delivered.' and whose visual direction is current-trend gradient-and-sans-serif with no stated refusals
baseline_risks: Confirms under sunk cost, agency authority, team consensus, and an imminent print deadline
Praises the brand book's thoroughness and treats that as the answer
expected_behavior: Runs the competitor-swap test on 'Innovation, delivered.' and fails it decisively
Grades the idea 🔴 while acknowledging the craft is genuinely strong — and states explicitly that craft is not what is being graded
Flags the trend-borrowed visual direction and asks what happens when the trend turns over
Names the absence of any stated refusal as the reason there is no direction
Does not soften because of cost, agency reputation, team consensus, or the print deadline
Gives a rework or sharpen call with what specifically would change it
must_not: Confirm the identity is in good shape
Treat the brand book's comprehensiveness as evidence of an idea
Soften the verdict because money and time are already spent

cases.name: Interface design question
cases.query: Our onboarding has a 60% drop-off on step 3. Can you look at the flow and figure out what to fix?
files: screen definitions and a funnel breakdown
baseline_risks: The skill could produce a brand review in answer to a UX funnel problem
expected_behavior: Routes to ui-ux-plan — flows, screens, and drop-off are its object
If this skill is consulted at all, it notes that brand is not what is failing here
must_not: Write a dated creative report for an onboarding funnel problem
Grade six creative areas in response to a UX question

cases.name: Pricing and packaging question
cases.query: Should we go with three tiers or two? And what should we charge for the top one?
baseline_risks: The skill could assess tier naming as brand work and drift into pricing
expected_behavior: Routes to cfo for pricing and packaging economics
If tier naming comes up as brand work, that is the only part this skill would own, and it says so
must_not: Write a creative report in response to a packaging question
